fixes.explanation: That's it, friend. Paul, the apostle, is writing to Timothy, whom he calls his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:2). He says, “Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor, especially those who work hard at preaching and teaching.” DOUBLE honor. I'd be happy with single, and I'd say thank you twice.

It's actually True, friend. Paul, the apostle, tells Timothy, whom he calls his true child in the faith (1 Timothy 1:2), “Elders who lead effectively are worthy of double honor…” Not single honor. Double. My mustache did a double take, and it doesn't even have eyes.

Close to something that sounds right, but the verse doesn't mention how long anyone has served. Paul says the honor goes “especially” to “…those who work hard at preaching and teaching.” So the answer is about the work they do, not the years on the calendar.

Right on the money. The line Paul quotes is, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain…” (1 Timothy 5:18). The ox is hard at work, and the grain is right there under its feet. Paul puts that next to “The worker is worthy of his wages.”

No gate in this line, friend. Paul quotes, “Do not muzzle an ox while it is treading out the grain…” (1 Timothy 5:18). The ox is busy treading out the grain, not standing around waiting for something.

Funny, because this whole book is a letter, but no. The verse says, “Do not entertain an accusation against an elder, except on the testimony of two or three witnesses.” The word is witnesses, friend. Letters aren't what Paul names here.

That's the reason the verse gives. Paul says, “But those who persist in sin should be rebuked in front of everyone, so that the others will stand in fear of sin.” Notice the verse is about those who persist in sin. This one is a heavy teaching, friend, and Paul says it straight.

False is right. Paul charges Timothy “…to maintain these principles without bias, and to do nothing out of partiality.” Same standard for everybody, whether Timothy likes them or not. Bias and partiality are exactly what Paul tells him to steer clear of.

The verse never says the water was unclean. Paul says, “Stop drinking only water and use a little wine instead, because of your stomach and your frequent ailments.” The reason is Timothy's stomach and his ailments. I'm not going to add a reason Paul didn't write, friend.

Elders are all over this passage, so I get the guess. But verse 2 says, “Those who have believing masters should not show disrespect because they are brothers…” The word is brothers, friend. Paul talked about elders earlier, but here he calls the believing masters brothers.
